messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a tail-latency spike right after landing the smaller minibatch timer change. 95th jumped ~2.3x on the qps test run. Anyone digging into why the timer drift causes extra work?

samir: I pulled a quick perf profile. Looks like kernel selection is flipping to the generic fp32 matmul path when micro-batch sizes hit the boundary. That increases register pressure and kills sustained throughput. Flame graph attached (short summary below).

marta: can you paste the config we switched to? wondering if token_budget or the interval moved us into a different kernel heuristics bucket.

samir: sure — snippet from the test harness config:

```json
{"minibatch_ms": 6, "coalesce_delay_ms": 14, "jitter_ms": 3, "token_budget": 1024, "queue_policy": "fifo"}
```

samir: when minibatch_ms goes below ~8ms we sometimes end up with micro-batches of 1-2 sequences which triggers the fallback kernels. The runtime's kernel selector currently checks avg_batch_tokens and seq_len distribution; the boundary math is a bit brittle.

devon: infra-bot just posted the alert during the run: infra-bot: [ALERT] service/redwood-runtime latency_p95 > 250ms for 5m. auto-roll attempted. :alarm_clock:  

nina: also saw elevated KV cache miss rate at the same time. If scans are misaligned and micro-batch boundaries split cached prefixes, we pump more compute. Misses went from 2%->9% on the problematic runs.

alex: interesting — so two amplification routes: kernel fallback + KV cache churn. We should profile end-to-end: kernel counters + KV hit/miss + batch size histogram.

samir: I exported a small report:
- avg_seq_per_microbatch: 1.8 (target 4-8)
- median_tokens_per_batch: 420
- kernel_path_switches/sec: 18 (baseline ~3)
- kv_cache_miss_pct: 8.7% (baseline 2.1%)

marta: concrete suggestion: raise minibatch_ms floor to 10ms in the short term to stabilize kernel selection, and switch queue_policy to "opportunistic-priority" for small-high-qps routes. That should increase avg_seq_per_microbatch.

devon: I can push a quick experiment toggle:
```yaml
runtime.tuning.minibatch_ms: 10
runtime.tuning.coalesce_delay_ms: 12
runtime.tuning.jitter_ms: 5
runtime.tuning.queue_policy: opportunistic-priority
```

nina: on jitter — uniform jitter is currently symmetric and can create synchronized microbursts. We tried an exponential jitter in a perf sim earlier and it smoothed arrivals better. Worth trying: `jitter_distribution: exponential(lambda=0.25)` to bias small delays but keep occasional larger gaps.

samir: +1, exponential will reduce the probability of many nodes aligning at the same offset. Also we should make token_budget adaptive: scale target by recent kv_cache_hit_rate (if cache hit drops, reduce token_budget to avoid oversized batches that split prefixes).

alex: action items: 1) devon roll the minibatch_ms=10 + queue change to the canary pool (devon), 2) samir add kernel-selector logging for boundary cases and attach kernel id in traces (samir), 3) nina run a jitter dist comparison sim and push results in this thread (nina), 4) marta create an alert/auto-tune playbook entry so we don't flip the wrong knobs manually (marta).

devon: starting canary deploy now, will post results in ~30m. rolling to 3 nodes with low qps first.

infra-bot: deployment/dev-canary-12 started by devon at 1819877601. status: in_progress

devon: canary finished — p95 back down to expected range, kernel_path_switches/sec dropped to 4, kv_cache_miss_pct -> 2.5%. looks promising.

marta: I'll draft the playbook and add a short experiment doc summarizing the probe thresholds for kernel selector boundaries.

nina: running the jitter sim now, will post numbers and a small plot link. initial runs show exponential jitter reduces 95th variance by ~15% vs uniform.

alex: great work. once nina posts sim result + samir's logs we can promote the change and open a follow-up to make token_budget adaptive. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
